item.title: Leavitt and Ocasio-Cortez spark conversation on challenges of family and career
item.summary: # US women in politics spark conversation about balancing family and career Last summer, Representative Sara Jacobs would run up to her office to give herself injections of hormones before rushing back to Congress for a session with her fellow lawmakers. The shots were for the second round of freezing her eggs, a medical procedure that can give women more time to have children. "It was an empowering decision that gave me more agency," the 37-year-old said, adding that the process was challenging. "Your body hurts. Your hormones are crazy. It's kind of like puberty and menopause at the same time," she said. Jacobs announced she was beginning the egg freezing process in 2021, at a time where she said few lawmakers were discussing the topic in the halls of Congress. The process - which can cost more than $10,000 and is rarely covered by insurance - involves doctors harvesting eggs from the ovaries and freezing them for a future pregnancy.
